skill.name: localhero
skill.description: Manages i18n translations with Localhero.ai. Use when working with translation files, adding user-facing strings, or modifying UI copy.
skill.summary: Manage source strings and translation workflows with Localhero.ai.
skill.author: localheroai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown false positives involving inline code, example identifiers, and legitimate Localhero.ai links. The skill does direct agents to execute an external npm package, upload source strings, and handle an API key, including one unsafe command-line option.

remediation.issue: The skill executes @localheroai/cli through npx without a pinned version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited CLI version and require user confirmation before commands that upload or modify files.

remediation.issue: Authentication guidance permits passing an API key as a command argument.
remediation.suggestion: Remove command-line key guidance and recommend a protected environment variable or secret manager.

remediation.issue: Translation commands may upload source strings to Localhero.ai.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose uploaded data and request confirmation before sending project content to the external service.

remediation.issue: The CLI reference advises removing a stale credential file.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before deleting .localhero_key and provide a non-destructive credential selection option.

content.value_statement: Internationalized projects need consistent source strings, keys, glossary terms, and translation updates. This skill applies project conventions and runs Localhero.ai workflows.
actual_capabilities: Reads localhero.json to identify source locales and translation directories.
Examines existing files before creating or changing localization keys.
Uses Localhero glossary and project settings when writing source copy.
Supports JSON, YAML, PO, and POT localization conventions.
Runs Localhero CLI workflows for translation, glossary, settings, login, and setup.
limitations: Requires an existing Localhero.ai account and authenticated CLI for service operations.
Relies on the external @localheroai/cli package and Localhero.ai availability.
Does not independently verify generated translation quality.
Translation commands may send project source strings to Localhero.ai.

use_cases.title: Add Product Interface Copy
use_cases.description: Add source-language labels and messages while preserving the application naming pattern and voice.

use_cases.title: Maintain Localization Consistency
use_cases.description: Apply approved glossary terms and project style settings across new interface strings.

use_cases.title: Configure Monorepo Translation Paths
use_cases.description: Review translation directories and coordinate Localhero workflows across multiple applications.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Source String
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a source-language string for [interface element]. Follow the existing localization key pattern and do not write target-language values.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one localized interface string.

prompt_templates.title: Update Feature Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the source copy for [feature]. Review localhero.json, existing keys, glossary terms, and project style before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is revising several related messages.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Translation Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review changed source strings for [branch]. Explain the translation workflow, then request approval before running external Localhero commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants a controlled translation update.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Monorepo Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit Localhero configuration across [applications]. Compare translation paths, key conventions, workflow triggers, glossary use, and missing translation risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A platform team needs a cross-application localization review.

best_practices: Review localhero.json and existing source files before changing localization keys.
Use project glossary terms and style settings consistently.
Confirm external CLI operations before uploading content or modifying translation files.
anti_patterns: Do not write target-language values directly when Localhero manages them.
Do not pass API keys through command arguments or expose credential files.
Do not run broad translation commands before checking automated workflows and changed files.

faq.question: What files does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It reviews localhero.json, configured source translation files, and relevant GitHub workflow files.

faq.question: Does it write translated languages?
faq.answer: No. It writes source-language strings and delegates target translation to Localhero.ai.

faq.question: Which localization formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers JSON, YAML, PO, and POT conventions used by the project.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. Localhero CLI operations contact Localhero.ai for authentication, project settings, glossary data, and translations.

faq.question: How should API keys be provided?
faq.answer: Use a protected environment variable or secret manager. Avoid command arguments because they may expose credentials.

faq.question: Can it support multiple applications?
faq.answer: Yes. One localhero.json can define multiple translation directories that share project settings and target languages.
